Class ScreenPanelAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.inject.ScreenPanelAdapter
public final class ScreenPanelAdapter extends Object
Renders a Panel inside a vanilla container screen and dispatches input to it. Constructing an adapter registers it; the library renders the panel and routes clicks on every targeted screen with no consumer mixin. 
Panel panel = Panel.builder("mymod:controls")
        .add(new Button(0, 0, 90, 16, Component.literal("Press"), b -> {}))
        .build();
new ScreenPanelAdapter(panel, MenuRegion.RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP.priority(10))
        .on(InventoryScreen.class);

Targeting: with no on(Class...) or onAny() call the panel renders on every container screen. unregister() removes it. A consumer-owned mixin may instead call render(GuiGraphicsExtractor, ScreenBounds, int, int, AbstractContainerScreen) and mouseClicked(ScreenBounds, double, double, int, AbstractContainerScreen) directly for a pixel-positioned panel; that path does not require targeting.

Context-parity with other rendering contexts

This adapter renders panels identically to the other two MenuKit rendering contexts (standalone MKScreen, HUD MKHudPanel):
  • PanelStyle auto-render. When the wrapped panel's style is not PanelStyle.NONE, the adapter paints the panel background before rendering elements. Consumers previously had to render backgrounds themselves; they don't anymore.
  • Content padding. Elements render inside a padded content area. Padding defaults to DEFAULT_PADDING (matches MKScreen.PANEL_PADDING) — set explicitly via the padding constructor parameter, including 0 for flush-edge behavior.

These defaults may shift the visual output of panels that were constructed against the pre-12.5 adapter (no background, no padding). Consumer mods migrate during Phase 13a by either declaring PanelStyle.NONE explicitly + passing padding=0, or adjusting their origin functions to account for the new padded content offset. See menukit/Design Docs/Phase 12/M5_REGION_SYSTEM.md §12.5a addendum.

Scope — what the adapter bundles, what it doesn't

The adapter bundles the mechanical parts of injection:
  • Coordinate translation. The panel's screen-space origin is resolved from its declared MenuRegion and the vanilla screen's bounds via RegionRegistry.resolveMenuOrigin(Panel, MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, AbstractContainerScreen). The adapter resolves it per frame so resizes are handled automatically.
  • Panel-background rendering. When panel.getStyle() != NONE, paints the styled background at the panel's origin with padding-inclusive dimensions.
  • Render dispatch. Constructs the RenderContext with the padded content origin and mouse coords, iterates visible elements, and calls element.render(ctx).
  • Input dispatch. Translates mouse coordinates with padding applied, hit-tests each visible element against its bounds, and dispatches mouseClicked to elements under the cursor. Returns whether any element consumed the click.
The adapter explicitly does not bundle policy decisions:
  • Visibility composition. The consumer decides whether to call adapter.render(...) and adapter.mouseClicked(...) at all. Visibility is either owned by Panel's own supplier (set via Panel.showWhen(BooleanSupplier)) or by the consumer's own predicates layered in the mixin. The adapter short-circuits when !panel.isVisible() but does not manage visibility itself.
  • Click cancellation. mouseClicked(ScreenBounds, double, double, int, AbstractContainerScreen) returns whether the click landed on an interactive element; the consumer's mixin inspects the return value and decides whether to cancel vanilla's handling.

Lifecycle with the mixin

The adapter is held as a @Unique final field on the consumer's mixin. A single adapter instance lives for the lifetime of the vanilla screen's class. The Panel it wraps is typically a static field on the consumer's mod class — one Panel per visual group, constructed once at mod init.
See Also:
  • The visual unit being injected
  • Vanilla-screen layout snapshot passed per call

  • Constructor Details

    • ScreenPanelAdapter

      public ScreenPanelAdapter(Panel panel, MenuRegion region, int padding)
      Region-aware constructor with explicit padding. Registers the panel into the given MenuRegion via RegionRegistry with the declared padding so stacking math and overflow checks both account for it. Uses RegionAnchor.DEFAULT_PRIORITY for sibling ordering; pair with the RegionAnchor constructor below for explicit priority.

      Per-instance lifecycle: construct adapters typically as a static final field at mod init. For test/verification or runtime UI swaps, call unregister() when done. See M5 design doc §6.1.

    • ScreenPanelAdapter

      public ScreenPanelAdapter(Panel panel, RegionAnchor<MenuRegion> anchor)
      Region-aware constructor accepting a RegionAnchor — region paired with an explicit stacking priority. Use when sibling panels in the same region need deterministic ordering relative to each other (e.g., MenuRegion.RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP.priority(50)).

      Padding defers to Panel.interiorPadding() — 0 for PanelStyle.NONE (element edge = panel edge), DEFAULT_PADDING for styled panels. Consumers who want a different value pass it via the explicit-padding constructor overload.

    • ScreenPanelAdapter

      public ScreenPanelAdapter(Panel panel, int padding)
      Pixel-positioned constructor (§0057 Revision — the precision escape). The panel must declare PanelPosition.pixel(Supplier): its per-frame supplier is the origin authority, so there is no region — the panel never registers into region stacking (it doesn't stack; it sits at exactly the supplied coordinates) and the reactive wrap/scroll budgets are never fed (pixel placement = the consumer owns the exact geometry). Render, input, hover-suppression, and opacity all ride the same machinery as a region panel — only the origin source differs.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the panel's position is not PanelPosition.pixel(...) — a loud fail beats a silently unresolvable placement (the A4 rule)

  • Method Details

    • unregister

      public void unregister()
      Phase 16j R5 — removes this adapter from every internal registry collection: the per-region MENU list, the per-screen match cache, and the PENDING/REGISTERED tracking sets. After unregister() the adapter contributes nothing to layout, dispatch, or rendering.

      Intended for code paths that construct adapters outside mod-init (test/verification, runtime UI swaps, hot-reload-style workflows). Most consumers don't need this — they construct adapters as static final fields and never unregister.

      Idempotent: calling unregister() twice is safe. The adapter object itself is not reusable after unregister — to resume a registration, construct a new adapter.

      Note: the underlying Panel can be reused with a new adapter after this; the panel itself isn't owned by the adapter. Per-Panel metadata (priority, modId, padding) was cleared by RegionRegistry.unregisterMenu(Panel), so re-registering picks up fresh values from the new constructor call.

    • on

      @SafeVarargs public final ScreenPanelAdapter on(Class<? extends net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?>>... screenClasses)
      Declares the screen classes this adapter applies to. Resolution is class-ancestry — the adapter fires on any opened AbstractContainerScreen that is an instance of one or more of screenClasses. A consumer targeting ChestScreen.class thus covers modded subclasses (e.g., DoubleChestScreen extends ChestScreen).

      Multi-target semantics are OR — any matching target fires the adapter. Example: .on(InventoryScreen.class, CreativeModeInventoryScreen.class) covers both the survival and creative player-inventory screens (and modded subclasses of either).

      Player inventory (§0051): InventoryScreen (survival) and CreativeModeInventoryScreen (creative) are sibling classes — neither extends the other — so .on(InventoryScreen.class) alone is survival-only and silently misses creative. Use onPlayerInventory() to target the player inventory in both modes.

      Call exactly once per adapter. Duplicate declarations throw IllegalStateException. Use onAny() for the "every screen" shape; don't pass AbstractContainerScreen.class here.

      Parameters:
      screenClasses - one or more screen classes; must not be empty
      Returns:
      this adapter, for chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if targeting was already declared
      IllegalArgumentException - if screenClasses is empty

    • onAny

      public ScreenPanelAdapter onAny()
      Declares this adapter fires on every opened AbstractContainerScreen, including CreativeModeInventoryScreen, modded screens, and future screen classes. Explicit "every screen" intent — different from .on(AbstractContainerScreen.class) at the documentation level (though functionally identical via class-ancestry). Use .on(Class...) when the consumer wants a specific set of screens; .onAny() when they genuinely mean "everywhere."

      This is also the implicit default: a region-based adapter that declares no targeting at all is promoted to onAny() at the first- screen checkpoint (ScreenPanelRegistry.applyEverywhereDefault()). Calling onAny() only makes that intent explicit; to render on fewer screens, narrow with .on(...) / .onPlayerInventory() / .onMatching(ScreenMatcher.allExcept(...)) instead.

      Returns:
      this adapter, for chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if targeting was already declared

    • onPlayerInventory

      public ScreenPanelAdapter onPlayerInventory()
      Declares this adapter fires on the player inventory in both game modes — the survival InventoryScreen and the creative CreativeModeInventoryScreen. The two are sibling classes (neither extends the other), so .on(InventoryScreen.class) alone is survival-only and silently misses creative (§0051). This is the turnkey both-modes target, so a consumer decorating the player inventory cannot accidentally ship a survival-only panel.

      An opt-out narrowing from the everywhere default (see onAny()): call this when a panel belongs only on the player inventory, not on every container.

      Equivalent to .on(InventoryScreen.class, CreativeModeInventoryScreen.class).

      Returns:
      this adapter, for chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if targeting was already declared

    • onMatching

      public ScreenPanelAdapter onMatching(ScreenMatcher matcher)
      Declares this adapter fires on every screen a ScreenMatcher accepts — the parity-shaped targeting mode. Where on(Class...) is an explicit class list and onAny() is unconditional, this delegates the per-screen decision to the matcher, so ScreenMatcher.all() (default-on everywhere) with a ScreenMatcher.allExcept(Class...) opt-out is expressible as a single targeting declaration.

      This is the seam the container-parity registration (MKCContainerPanel) uses to wire a registered panel's chrome: one parity scope drives both the slot projection (MKC side) and the chrome targeting (here), so the two cannot drift.

      Parameters:
      matcher - the screen scope; must be non-null
      Returns:
      this adapter, for chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if targeting was already declared

    • isTargetingDeclared

    • matches

      public boolean matches(Class<? extends net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?>> screenClass)
      Tests whether this adapter's declared targets match the given opened screen class. An adapter that hasn't declared targeting returns false only transiently — the first-screen checkpoint (ScreenPanelRegistry.applyEverywhereDefault()) promotes it to onAny() (every container) before dispatch, so by the time this is consulted an undeclared adapter matches all. Step 3's registry dispatch uses this to filter matching adapters per screen open.

    • getOrigin

      public Optional<ScreenOrigin> getOrigin(ScreenBounds screenBounds, net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen)
      Returns the panel's screen-space origin (top-left corner of the background rectangle) for the given screen bounds, or empty when the panel is invisible or out-of-region.

      Added in Phase 12.5 (V4 finding) so consumers rendering sibling decorations alongside the adapter's panel (tooltips, hover overlays, related info panels) don't re-derive origin math from RegionMath. The content area begins at origin + getPadding().

      Takes the live screen instance so chrome-aware region resolution can consult MenuChrome.

    • render

      public void render(net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiGraphicsExtractor graphics, ScreenBounds screenBounds, int mouseX, int mouseY, net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen)
      Renders the panel background (when style is not PanelStyle.NONE) and the panel's visible elements at the origin computed from the given screen bounds. No-op when !panel.isVisible() or when the region-aware origin resolver returns out-of-region.

      screen is passed through to the region resolver so chrome-aware region resolution can consult MenuChrome.

    • mouseClicked

      public boolean mouseClicked(ScreenBounds screenBounds, double mouseX, double mouseY, int button, net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen)
      Dispatches a mouse click to any visible element under the cursor. No-op (returns false) when !panel.isVisible() or out-of-region.

      Hit-testing uses padded content origin so element bounds line up with where the elements actually rendered. screen is threaded to the region resolver for chrome-aware region resolution parity with render(GuiGraphicsExtractor, ScreenBounds, int, int, AbstractContainerScreen).

      Returns:
      true if an element consumed the click.

    • mouseScrolled

      public boolean mouseScrolled(ScreenBounds screenBounds, double mouseX, double mouseY, double scrollX, double scrollY, net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen)
      Dispatches a mouse-wheel scroll to any visible element under the cursor. Same hit-test logic as mouseClicked(ScreenBounds, double, double, int, AbstractContainerScreen); returns whether any element consumed the scroll.

      Added in Phase 14d-2 alongside ScrollContainer — the first element kind that consumes scroll input. Existing elements default false and pass through.

      Returns:
      true if an element consumed the scroll.

    • mouseReleased

      public boolean mouseReleased(ScreenBounds screenBounds, double mouseX, double mouseY, int button, net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen)
      Dispatches a mouse-release event to all visible elements. Unlike mouseClicked(ScreenBounds, double, double, int, AbstractContainerScreen), this is NOT hit-tested against element bounds — release fires for every visible element so drag-end detection works when the cursor has moved off the element during drag.

      Added in Phase 14d-2 alongside ScrollContainer for scrollbar-drag end detection. Existing elements default false.

    • keyPressed

      public boolean keyPressed(int keyCode, int scanCode, int modifiers)
      Dispatches a key press to this adapter's visible elements (keyboard-nav completion — the keyboard parallel to mouseClicked(ScreenBounds, double, double, int, AbstractContainerScreen)). NOT hit-tested: keyboard events aren't localized to a cursor position, so every visible element is offered the key until one consumes it. Returns true once an element consumes, so the caller eats the key from vanilla. Canonical consumer: an open Dropdown.
